brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 3 spikes variant stud placed at junctions spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0 ; spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 ; spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0
all three placed with facing down

finish.summary: Seven-cell honeycomb built from 7 full bases in classic hex cluster, raised on 3 stud spikes facing down distributed across the honeycomb footprint. Open faces capped and joints locked.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your seven-cell honeycomb on stud-spike feet — I'll build it and get it standing.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
